messages.author: aabece9c4e8a3597
messages.subject: Avro bindings for RHIPE?
parts:
I am building java+scala bridges to R that have a lot in common with
the RHIPE reqts.
I will definitely use RHIPE as soon as I have access to a HadoopFS
setup!
Until then (and even after then when I'm in "local experiment" mode),
I would like to
use Java mappings that are as compatible with RHIPE as possible (so R
+Java
experiments will run "the same way", semantically, using local JVM vs.
Hadoop cloud).

In Saptarshi's presentation of 2010-08-13, on Todo slide 24, he asks,
"Move to Avro serialization?" I wouldn't want anyone to have to
"move",
necessarily, but it would be very nice to have Avro-Java bindings for
R!

Do others in the R + Hadoop community see large potential benefit in
having
Avro available as a channel (in addition to protobuf, at least at
first)?
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Why I care, in case you care:

We have committed to using Avro as the serialization format for the
following projects,
which will all benefit from connectivity to R (as well as Hadoop):

www.appdapter.org, www.cogchar.org, www.robokind.org <-
Apache license.
www.bucksum.com <- financial, closed source for now.

We have Avro serialization working over QPid, but have not tried it
yet with Hadoop.
We chose Avro in part because we like the design, in part because we
have expected
Avro to become the best way to serialize for Hadoop. I recognize that
not all of Hadoop
has been bound to Avro yet, but I am not current on the details; I
assume Avro
is still the long term strategic direction. True?

We could contribute to an effort to make RHIPE more Avro friendly, if
others are interested.

peace,

Stu

messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] Avro bindings for RHIPE?

I wanted to move to Avro because I was under the impression that
Hadoop and Avro would be very tightly interlinked. I have played with
Avro and wrote something similar to Protocol representations. However,
though the mailing list is very helpful I find Avro documentation
lacking. Things petered out on my end.

Best asked on the Avro mailing list.

>
> We could contribute to an effort to make RHIPE more Avro friendly, if
> others are interested.
>

Since I have stumbled and paused on writing a splittable input format
(like SequenceFiles) based on protocol buffers (i.e can be created in
other languages unlike ProtocolBuffers), I'm happy to see Avro used.

However, Protocol Buffers is used extensively and I haven't wrapped
the PB api calls. PB is not just used for the streaming data
interchange, but also between R and the Java server. In summary, it's
very much all over the place.

I appreciate the time you have taken to ask these questions.

Cheers
Saptarshi
